intro: Public activity associated with Mohammad Zubair Mir in Baramulla has included political organisation, youth engagement, neighbourhood outreach, local sports initiatives and engagement with traders and civic concerns. This profile assembles those activities in a dated public record, with source links and evidence labels wherever available.

sections.title: Education and public background
paragraphs: Mir's stated academic background is in Money, Banking and Finance at the University of Exeter in the United Kingdom. The precise qualification title should be confirmed against the original academic document before this wording is treated as a verified credential.
His public-facing activity identified for this archive is centred on Baramulla and includes political and community engagement across urban neighbourhoods and surrounding localities.

sections.title: Political organisation and youth engagement
paragraphs: Media coverage in 2025 documented youth-focused political activity in Baramulla, including a youth meeting in Old Town and a youth convention associated with the Youth People's Conference. A local report in December 2025 described Mir as District President of the Youth People's Conference, Baramulla.
The activity record also includes several political joining events. This archive records those events collectively and does not list individual participants' names.

A public-facing profile should distinguish a reported office at a particular date from a current appointment. The December 2025 designation is therefore presented as a dated media report unless a newer authoritative confirmation is added.

sections.title: Neighbourhood outreach and follow-up assistance
paragraphs: The material assembled for this profile describes a pattern of initial community meetings followed by return visits and practical follow-up. Locations identified include Dardpora, Sangri, Gutiyar, Jal Sheeri, Narwa and Odoora, as well as Old Town neighbourhoods.

In Sangri, public posts and local reporting identified for this archive refer to streetlight-related assistance in Sangri Ward. A report attributed the provision to personal funds; the quantity, cost and funding details have not been independently audited here.

A post titled “Shukriya Sangri”, dated 12 May 2026, is part of the activity record. The account supplied for this profile also describes a larger Sangri programme and follow-up assistance. Attendance figures should remain estimates unless supported by an independently verified count.
Gutiyar is included because a public post was identified as referring to lighting assistance there. The direct post URL and date should be attached before the detail is treated as fully sourced.
For Dardpora, the record describes outreach followed by a return visit with streetlights and other items. The precise date and original post should be linked before publication as a verified event.

sections.title: Old Town and surrounding localities
paragraphs: The Old Town activity record includes Qazi Hamam, Gulnar Park and Kakarhamam. Kakarhamam is treated here as a neighbourhood within Old Town, not as a separate village.

Other locality-level entries include Jal Sheeri and the Narwa Block area. The Narwa Block meeting record refers to Odoora, Namblan, Khal and nearby villages. Locality spellings should follow the original source material; this archive uses Narwa and Odoora as supplied for the profile.

sections.title: Youth sports and community sport
paragraphs: Sports-related activity includes the People's Cup, reported in September 2025, and involvement with Sultan Warriors. A public post dated 15 September 2026 reportedly marked the team's Chinar Premier League final win; the exact role title associated with the team should be checked against the original post.

The supplied activity record also refers to volleyball equipment support, local football support involving Sheeri Blues CF, and attendance as a special guest at the Balkote Uri Volleyball Smash Bash 2026. Add direct source links and event dates to each entry as they are verified.

sections.title: Engagement with traders and civic concerns
paragraphs: The record includes a meeting with the GMC Kantbagh Trader Federation, dated around 26 July 2026 in the material supplied for this archive. The original public post should be linked to confirm the date and the meeting's stated purpose.

Public commentary associated with the profile has addressed employment and recruitment, roads and infrastructure, food safety, local economic concerns and accountability. Individual statements should be linked to their original publication so readers can assess the wording and context.

editorial_policy: This is an independent public-information archive, not an official biography or a party/subject website.
Third-person writing does not mean independent eyewitness verification. Each entry identifies its evidence type and verification status.
Media reports, original social-media posts, organiser records and contributor-supplied accounts are not interchangeable. Label them accurately.
Do not state estimated crowd sizes as verified counts. If included, attribute estimates to the source and explain how they were estimated.
Do not claim that assistance was personally funded unless a reliable source supports that claim. Do not state quantities or costs without documentation.
Do not publish names of political joiners merely to make an event appear larger. Keep collective descriptions unless names are already public and there is a sound editorial reason to include them.
Confirm current political titles before presenting them as current. Preserve historical titles with their date and source.
Obtain permission for portraits and avoid publishing private contact details or sensitive personal information.
